Technical & price structure: In plain terms: the operating fertilizer plants are worth ~EGP 54bn; add ~EGP 16bn net cash and ~EGP 6bn of investments and equity is ~EGP 60 a share. Far more cash than debt. The whole argument is whether subsidised gas holds — and the ~9–10% dividend pays you to wait.
Monte Carlo — where could the price go?: 50,000 paths, 16 forces: the gas-feedstock cost (the dominant swing), the EGP, global urea/ammonia prices, rates, inflation, foreign flows, dividend policy and gas-supply interruptions. Details in the methodology .
FAQ: What is the fair-value range for Abu Kir Fertilizers (ABUK)? — testahil publishes a probability distribution of where ABUK could trade over the next 1–3 months — the simulated 5th–95th percentile range and the central 50% — not a single price target or a buy/sell call. The full study and open model show the methodology. This is educational analysis, not investment advice.

How is the ABUK valuation calculated? — The study uses an instrument-appropriate lens — a sum-of-the-parts / RNAV build for a real-estate developer — combined with a 50,000-path Monte Carlo simulation that expresses the result as a probability distribution. Every assumption is visible and editable in the free Excel model.

Does testahil recommend buying or selling ABUK? — No. testahil never issues buy, sell, or hold recommendations. It publishes fair-value ranges and probability distributions as educational material, and grades its own forecasts publicly when they resolve.
